# Belinda

## Overview

- **Age:** Fourteen years old
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049)</sub>
- **Role:** Servant girl and companion to Miss Rosalind Penrose  <sub>[v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043)</sub>
- **Titles:** Belinda the Fourth  <sub>[v2 c21 P46](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0046), [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Belinda the Fourth  <sub>[v2 c21 P46](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0046), [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049)</sub>

## Appearance

She is the final and finest daughter among the Bowman sisters. She attempts in front of her mirror to mirror the posture, walk, and expressions of Nell Harcourt.

_Sources: [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039)_

## Personality

Belinda is an obliging, attentive, and deeply compassionate servant girl who holds immense admiration for Nell. She is loyal and tolerant of Miss Rosalind Penrose's imaginative games, refraining from calling her foolish. Gentle and sensitive, she becomes deeply anxious when she senses her mistress's declining health and sadness.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044)_

## History

Belinda the Fourth serves as a young live-in helper to Miss Rosalind Penrose at Echo Cottage. When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke wander off their path, Miss Rosalind and Belinda host them for tea, serving warm biscuits and mother's wedding china. Unlike the previous Bowman daughters who served as Charlottas, Belinda never mocks Miss Rosalind's pretend tea parties or imaginative games. She holds Nell in total adoration, practicing in her bedroom mirror to imitate Nell's walk, posture, and facial expressions. When wild strawberries ripen in Mr. Kimball's pasture, Belinda invites Nell to join her in picking them for afternoon tea. During this outing, she confides her deep worry to Nell that Miss Rosalind has been sick and lonely ever since taking a cold during a winter evening walk.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c21 P61](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0061), [v2 c27 P37](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0037), [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044)_
